A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReHub study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReHub benchmark results, memory measurements, component ablations, and sensitivity and hub-utilization analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds experiments comparing random and balanced random alternatives for clustering and hub assignment.

M1.justification: ReHub's initialization, five update steps, reassignment algorithm, and prediction procedures remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. The new balanced random algorithm is an experimental comparator, not a replacement component of ReHub.

E1.justification: The reported molecular, superpixel, citation-network, and synthetic regular-graph evaluations retain the same dataset and task coverage. The new assignment experiments reuse PascalVOC-SP.

E2.justification: New Table 5 evaluates Random and Balanced Random alternatives for clustering, initial hub assignment, and reassignment. The external baseline sets in Tables 1–3 and the memory comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 5 introduces controlled comparisons that separately vary clustering, initial assignment, or reassignment while retaining PascalVOC-SP and k = 3. Previously reported training configurations and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; the added parameter counts disclose existing configurations.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds a focused ablation testing whether random or approximately balanced connections can replace ReHub's structured assignments. Existing component ablations, hub-ratio sensitivity tests, and hub-utilization analyses are retained, including those in Appendix A.4.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations over five runs with different random seeds. The added ablation follows the existing reporting practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: New Table 5 adds six randomized-control results, with PascalVOC-SP F1 means from 0.3486 to 0.3622, compared with the retained ReHub result of 0.3860 ± 0.0172. Scores in Tables 1–4 and the corresponding appendix component-ablation table are unchanged. Redesigned Figure 3 no longer prints the earlier utilization AUC summaries.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds the balanced random assignment formula and a proof that a stride coprime with the hub count visits every hub index. It also adds METIS preprocessing complexity bounds and their linear-time implication for sparse graphs. ReHub's existing mathematical formulation and attention-complexity argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain linear complexity, modular integration with MPNNs, improvement over Neural Atoms, competitive benchmark performance, and sparse performance comparable to the dense variant. The new controls support these retained contributions rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the randomized controls as evidence for meaningful spoke-hub relationships and explains why long-range capability and large-graph efficiency are evaluated separately. The conclusion removes the explicit acknowledgment that ReHub did not establish a new state of the art, while retaining the geometric-position limitation and future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds model parameter counts, Appendix A.3 specifies the balanced random control, and Section 4 clarifies that baseline results are taken from their original publications. The abstract now explicitly identifies code availability through the existing project webpage. These are documentation additions, not evidence of changed ReHub configurations.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to Neural Atoms, Exphormer, GraphGPS, and other approaches. The expanded METIS discussion uses an already cited reference.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, expands Sections 4.3 and A.3, updates author information, removes the acknowledgments, and relabels the limitations paragraph as future work. Most existing prose and the overall section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the document's typography, margins, author block, and placement of displays. Figure 1 gains graphical attention illustrations; Figure 3 changes from two cumulative unused-hub plots to four used-hub histograms. Table 5 and Algorithm 2 are added, and multiple appendix tables gain parameter-count fields.

improvement.justification: The new randomized controls in Table 5 better test the value of ReHub's assignment choices, while parameter counts, baseline provenance, and control implementation details improve transparency. The main results remain unchanged. Removing the explicit non-state-of-the-art caveat slightly weakens the limitations discussion, but the focused evidential and documentation gains support a modest net improvement.
